item.text: I’m checking a small set of Reuters, HRW, IMF/FATF, and Turkish official sources to pin down whether 2024 appointments were technocratic or patronage-driven. After that I’ll stop and synthesize only the strongest claim-level items.

item.text:
**Verdict:** Mixed, leaning negative. In 2024 Erdoğan did appoint some real professionals in macroeconomic roles, but the broader pattern was not merit-neutral: the media regulator, local administrators, and security/legal tools were used in ways that protected the ruling bloc and marginalized opposition actors. I did not find strong 2024 proof of a cabinet filled with family members or obvious business cronies, so the strongest negative evidence is about loyalists and partisan control rather than direct kinship patronage.

| Direction | Title | Publisher | Date | URL | Claim-level summary | QIDs |
|---|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| Positive | Press Release on the Appointment of CBRT Governor | Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye | 2024-02-04 | https://www.tcmb.gov.tr/wps/wcm/connect/en/tcmb%2Ben/main%2Bmenu/announcements/press%2Breleases/2024/ano2024-06 | Erdoğan appointed Fatih Karahan, a professional economist and former Fed/New York Fed staffer, as CBRT governor. That is solid evidence of at least one major appointment going to a competent technocrat rather than a family member or obvious crony. | 7B.5; 7B.4; 6B.9 |
| Positive | Turkey central bank chief resigns after aggressive rate hikes | Reuters | 2024-02-02 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/turkey-central-bank-chief-resigns-after-aggressive-rate-hikes-3291652 | Reuters described Karahan as a capable successor with a Fed background and said Şimşek’s program would continue uninterrupted. This supports a reading that Erdoğan still relied on professional economic managers where stabilization mattered. | 7B.5; 7B.4; 6B.9 |
| Positive | DMO foreword on transparency and digital procurement | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-05-03 | https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Eng/Home/EngIcerik/1212 | The state procurement agency says its system emphasizes transparency, competition, accountability, and digital e-tenders. That is evidence of a bureaucratic lane that is at least formally insulated from pure loyalist allocation. | 7B.5; 7B.4 |
| Positive | DMO Health Market expansion and savings | Devlet Malzeme Ofisi Genel Müdürlüğü | 2024-10-17 | https://www.dmo.gov.tr/Home/Icerik/3992 | DMO says centralized digital procurement covered most hospital drug and medical-supply demand and generated savings. This is a concrete example of rule-based service delivery instead of obvious patronage staffing. | 7B.5; 7B.4 |
| Negative | Turkey’s media landscape remains tightly controlled | Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism | 2024-06-17 | https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/turkey | The report says Erdoğan began the term with continued tight control over the media, with incumbents receiving disproportionate airtime and critical outlets facing regulatory pressure. That is strong evidence of staffing and institutional control favoring loyalists and regime protection. | 7B.5; 7B.2 |
| Negative | Turkey: Government Removes Elected Opposition Mayors | Human Rights Watch | 2024-11-07 | https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/11/07/turkiye-government-removes-elected-opposition-mayors | HRW says elected mayors were removed and replaced with state appointees using terrorism allegations. This is direct evidence that local governance roles were filled or overridden to neutralize political rivals, not just to maximize competence. | 7B.5; 7B.3; 7B.2 |
| Negative | Turkey replaces Kurdish mayor with government candidate two days after vote | Reuters | 2024-04-02 | https://uk.investing.com/news/world-news/prokurdish-party-challenges-election-outcomes-in-eastern-turkey-3412985 | Reuters reported authorities blocked a newly elected pro-Kurdish mayor from taking office and reran a district vote after the ruling party lost. That is strong evidence of using appointment and electoral administration to protect ruling-party power. | 7B.5; 7B.3 |
| Negative | Turkey unseats Kurdish mayors in crackdown after peace proposal | Reuters | 2024-11-04 | https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Turkey%2Bunseats%2BKurdish%2Bmayors%2Bin%2Bcrackdown%2Bafter%2Bpeace%2Bproposal/23918110.html | Reuters said three pro-Kurdish mayors were dismissed and replaced by government-appointed administrators. This reinforces that Erdoğan’s system kept using centrally controlled loyalist administrators when opposition figures won office. | 7B.5; 7B.3 |
| Negative | Turkey’s CB governor faces accusation of family influence on bank operations | Turkish Minute | 2024-01-18 | https://www.turkishminute.com/2024/01/18/turkeys-cb-governor-faces-accusation-of-family-influence-on-bank-operations/ | A formal complaint alleged the governor’s father influenced operations, personnel, and use of facilities at the central bank. This is not adjudicated proof, but it is directly relevant evidence that family influence was at least plausibly intruding into a key state institution. | 7B.5; 7B.4 |
| Negative | Freedom in the World 2024: Turkey | Freedom House | 2024 | https://freedomhouse.org/country/turkey/freedom-world/2024 | Freedom House says RTÜK is appointed by an AKP-controlled parliament and that authorities target critical journalists and outlets. That points to institutions being staffed and used in ways that protect incumbency rather than independent professionalism. | 7B.5; 7B.2 |

Search gap: I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Erdoğan openly stocked the cabinet with family members, close friends, or named business donors. The clearest available pattern is mixed: technocratic appointments in the central bank and procurement versus patronage-style control over media regulation, local administration, and opposition-held offices.
